title: 4 global bodies warn energy risks still cloud trade outlook
summary:
IEA, IMF, World Bank Group and WTO heads met recently under an April coordination group on Middle East war impacts.
They said energy markets and goods transit still face strains despite lower fuel and fertiliser prices since June.
Exporters, importers and sourcing teams should track navigation, port infrastructure and trade facilitation actions as agencies keep monitoring risks.

title: ICE cotton retreats from one-month high on profit booking
summary:
ICE cotton futures retreated from a one-month high as profit booking and a stronger US dollar weighed on prices.
The December 2026 contract settled at 80.67 cents/lb, though it remained higher for the week.
Rising crude oil prices, weaker US crop ratings, and cautious positioning ahead of key USDA reports helped limit losses, supporting overall market sentiment.

title: Asia-Pacific growth forecast cut to 4.9% for 2026: ADB
summary:
ADB has cut its 2026 growth forecast for developing Asia and the Pacific to 4.9 per cent from 5.5 per cent in 2025, citing Middle East conflict-driven energy market disruptions. 
It raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 4.3 per cent, while warning that geopolitical tensions, tighter financial conditions and trade uncertainty could further weigh on regional growth despite expected recovery in 2027.

title: OECD-wide employment expected to grow 0.3% in 2026, 0.6% in 2027
summary:
Job markets in OECD members have been resilient, with total employment in such nations at an all-time high and projected to continue to grow. 
However, real wages remain below their levels five years ago in around a third, and this year’s energy shock may put further pressure on wages, an OECD report revealed. 
OECD-wide employment is expected to grow by 0.3 per cent in 2026 and 0.6 per cent in 2027.

title: UK, Turkiye make progress in fifth round of FTA negotiations
summary:
The UK and Turkiye completed the fifth round of enhanced free trade agreement talks in Ankara, closing 11 chapters to date. 
Discussions covered goods market access, digital trade, investment, procurement, intellectual property and sustainability. 
For sourcing teams, the talks could shape future trade terms; a sixth round is expected in the autumn.

title: At 52.9, Bangladesh’s PMI stays in expansion territory in June
summary:
Bangladesh’s purchasing managers' index (PMI) stood at 52.9 in June this year, indicating continued growth in overall economic activity despite a slower pace month on month. 
The agriculture sector posted its tenth consecutive month of expansion, while the manufacturing and construction sectors saw a slower pace of activity in the month, but the PMI report was optimistic about future performance.

title: Deloitte cuts Australia's 2026-27 growth forecast to 1.3%
summary:
Deloitte Access Economics has cut Australia's 2026-27 real GDP growth forecast to 1.3 per cent from 1.9 per cent.
For textile and apparel exporters, weaker consumer spending and confidence point to a tougher demand setting.
Inflation and higher rates are squeezing households, with essential prices rising faster than headline CPI.

title: EIB Global backs Bangladesh's green shift with $68.4 mn
summary:
EIB Global and BRAC Bank PLC have agreed a €60 million (~$68.4 million), 12-year financing package for Bangladesh.
The facility targets green and circular investments, including a €20 million framework loan for ready-made garment, textile and export-focused sectors.
Suppliers serving EU buyers may gain longer-term funding to upgrade cleaner production and resource efficiency.

title: Indian CWG 2026 contingent to wear jute-viscose apparel
summary:

The blended fabric was developed with the support of Gloster Jute Mills, Kolkata. 
The apparel was designed by the National Institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi.

title: Australian apparel imports fall while textiles gain in July-May
summary:
Australia’s textile and apparel trade showed mixed trends in July–May FY2025-26.
Apparel imports fell 4.74 per cent to Au$11.62 billion, while textile yarn, fabric and fibre imports increased.
Textile fibre exports rose 6.74 per cent, although May imports of apparel, textiles and fibres declined year on year, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

title: EU’s July 19 compliance cliff rewrites global apparel sourcing
summary:
From July 19, brands selling into the EU can no longer destroy unsold apparel, while mandatory Digital Product Passports raise compliance across supply chains. 
With the EU accounting for 50.1 per cent of Bangladesh’s RMG exports ($19.7 billion), competitive advantage shifts from low-cost sourcing to demand forecasting, inventory precision and traceable data.

summary:
ILO and GFJTU held a three-day Amman workshop to strengthen migrant workers' representation in Jordan's trade unions.
Garment manufacturing was among sectors in focus, alongside construction, agriculture, services and domestic work.
Talks also covered fair recruitment, organising, grievance handling and access to justice for migrant workers.

title: Vietnam's textile & garment exports rise 0.9% to $18.8 bn in H1

Fabric imports grew 1.7 per cent to $7.67 billion, though cotton imports declined 3.1 per cent in value.
The country is targeting $50 billion in textile, garment, and yarn exports in 2026.

title: ‘FABRIC Cambodia II’ launched with German help amid tougher standards
summary:
Germany and Cambodia have launched phase II of a project to improve the latter’s garment, footwear and travel goods sector amid tougher global environmental and labour standards. 
FABRIC Cambodia II focuses on supply-chain transparency and compliance with global regulations, moving beyond factory-floor audits to embed sustainability through public-private policy dialogue and workforce training.

title: AAFA calls for no additional tariffs on footwear imported from Brazil
summary:
A top official of the American Apparel & Footwear Association recently testified at the USTR' Section 301 hearing on Brazil, urging against additional tariffs on footwear imported from there. 
Additional tariffs on Brazilian footwear would increase costs for American businesses and families without advancing the broader objectives of an American First trade policy,” he said.

title: Europe’s $256 bn apparel shift squeezes low-cost exporters
summary:

TexPro data showed the region’s apparel imports rose to $256.32 billion in 2025, but Q1 2026 slipped 3.5 per cent year-on-year (YoY).
Europe is still buying globally yet more of the value chain is being routed through EU hubs, stricter compliance systems, warehousing networks and parcel-level customs controls.

title: Bangladesh RMG exports down 1.6% to $38.7 bn in FY26; June rebounds
summary:

However, June exports rebounded strongly, rising 21.52 per cent year on year.
Home textile exports grew during both the fiscal year and June, while cotton product exports declined for the full year despite June gains.

summary:

Weak demand in the EU and US, falling prices and volumes, and rising policy risks highlight the need for exporters to diversify markets, upgrade products, and improve competitiveness beyond low-cost manufacturing.

Industry raised land access, policy uncertainty, and VAT pressure on local suppliers; the government sought tax relief proposals.
